RISE Lab · Current research

A self-calibrating digital twin for UR5e manipulation

The goal is a real-to-sim-to-real loop: use observations from a physical UR5e to improve its simulated twin, then use that twin to plan or train manipulation controllers for the real robot.

Current progress: The single-arm workstation scene has been built and verified in simulation. The next milestones are repeatable scripted manipulation and characterization of the simulated arm.

Research direction: Calibrate the twin against real observations, investigate online adaptation, and explore model predictive control, imitation learning, and reinforcement learning for manipulation.

Status: Physical calibration, controller transfer, and real-robot validation are future work. The earlier two-arm simulation established experience with coordinated manipulation and remains a benchmark.

Explore the digital twin repository · View earlier two-arm work

NAU undergraduate capstone · UGRADS

Shot difficulty and scoring across the NBA and NHL

How much of a player's shooting efficiency reflects the difficulty of the shots they take? This capstone uses matched 2014–2024 NBA and NHL shot data to study expected scoring, shot difficulty, and player performance.

Open full-resolution graph to zoom

My work: Developed data preparation and validation workflows, shot-quality models, a Shot Difficulty Index, and visual comparisons of player performance. The team presented the capstone at NAU UGRADS.

Isaac Sim Robotics System identification Sim-to-real

rise-two-arm-research

GitHub

Two-Arm Manipulation in Isaac Sim

Earlier RISE Lab simulation work coordinating two UR5e arms and RG2 grippers around a shared bar. This project provided a foundation for the single-arm digital twin research.

Python NVIDIA Isaac Sim USD Inverse kinematics
  • Added collision validation, joint-frame corrections, object-space goals, and per-arm inverse kinematics.
  • A 26-second simulation recorded four-finger contact at every measured sample, no unexpected collisions, and 0.135 mm maximum slip.
  • The two-arm work remains a simulation benchmark; it has not been validated on physical hardware.

NBA Shot Data Engineering Package

End-to-end NBA shot analytics package combining R data infrastructure with Python modeling workflows. The project supports multi-source ingestion, rerunnable SQLite updates, shot-quality modeling, and player-level archetype analysis.

R Python SQLite scikit-learn PyGAM Streamlit

nba-modeling

GitHub

Leakage-Aware NBA Win Modeling

Predicts NBA home wins using only information available before tip-off, with time-ordered validation and a companion R package, nba-data, that collects and validates ESPN game data. A scheduled job logs predictions for the current season before each game and scores them afterward.

R targets renv xgboost SQLite GitHub Actions
  • Tests check the features directly: changing one game's result changes no feature for that game or any earlier game.
  • On the held-out 2025-26 season the best model picked 68.6% of games correctly, against 55.4% for always picking the home team. Elo ratings alone reach 67.9%, and the interval for the gain from adding rolling features includes zero.
  • Corrected evaluation problems in an earlier course version, including cross-validation that mixed seasons and a threshold tuned on the test season, and documented each change.
  • Live 2026-27 predictions are scored on the project site; with only a few games played, early accuracy is not yet a conclusion.

ImageReconstruction

GitHub

Image Reconstruction and Generative Modeling

Research-style image reconstruction training project for MNIST-family datasets, covering autoencoders, denoising autoencoders, variational autoencoders, and diffusion models. The training pipeline is built for reproducibility, Slurm workflows, and GPU-backed HPC execution.

Python PyTorch Diffusion GPU training Slurm HPC workflows
  • Supports multiple model families from a single CLI with isolated outputs and saved run configuration.
  • Includes Slurm-safe dataset handling, run isolation, and GPU-oriented experiment workflows for shared compute environments.
  • Covers diffusion experiments, autoencoder baselines, and reproducible parameter sweeps for model comparison.

Halma Game AI

Turn-based game AI project that combines search, heuristics, and a local interface for interactive play and benchmarking. It is a clean example of autonomous decision-making logic implemented in a fully runnable system.

Python Minimax Alpha-beta pruning Tkinter Search heuristics
  • Implements minimax with optional alpha-beta pruning, move ordering, and iterative deepening.
  • Provides both a GUI surface and a headless arena for AI-vs-AI benchmarking.
  • Supports multiple board sizes and configurable per-move search budgets.
